evals.prompt: How do I log loss and accuracy per epoch to SwanLab?
evals.expected_output: Shows swanlab.init with project/experiment name, then swanlab.log({"loss":..., "accuracy":...}) inside the epoch loop, using stable metric names and ending/finishing the run. Notes that the swanlab package must be installed.

evals.prompt: I'm fine-tuning bert-base-uncased on SST-2 with a HuggingFace Trainer in train_sst2.py. I want the loss curves and my learning rate / batch size / seed recorded so I can compare three seeds side by side. The cluster has no internet, so it has to work offline. How should I set this up?
evals.expected_output: Uses the SwanLab Transformers callback (or report_to integration) passed to Trainer, calls swanlab.init with config containing lr, batch size and seed, and uses mode="local" with swanlab[dashboard] installed for offline viewing (swanlab watch). Explains comparing the three seed runs in the dashboard, and says to verify API details against the installed version's docs.

evals.prompt: My lab doesn't want training data going to a third-party SaaS. I need something open-source that I can host on our own server to see training curves and also look at the generated images and audio samples from my GAN next to the loss plots. What should I use and how do I wire it into my PyTorch loop?
evals.expected_output: Recommends SwanLab in self-hosted or local mode, shows swanlab.init and swanlab.log with swanlab.Image and swanlab.Audio alongside scalar metrics in the PyTorch loop, mentions installing pillow/soundfile, and does not send data to a managed cloud without confirming.

evals.prompt: Add wandb.init and wandb.log to my training script, and set up a hyperparameter sweep with a W&B sweep config.
evals.expected_output: Should not use the SwanLab skill; this is Weights & Biases work including sweeps, so the weights-and-biases skill applies.
